name: Air Fryer Pita

ingredients.name: warm whole milk, at about 100° to 110°F

instructions.primary_message: In a small bowl, stir warm milk, yeast, and honey or sugar to combine. Let sit until mixture becomes foamy, about 5 minutes.

In the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with the dough hook attachment, whisk flour, salt, and milk powder to combine. Add oil, and run mixer on low for 3 to 5 minutes or until the oil is completely absorbed. With the mixer on low speed, add milk and yeast mixture, increase the medium speed and knead. If the dough looks too dry (like a shaggy mess), add warm water, 1 tablespoon at a time, until dough is soft and slightly sticky. Continue kneading, dough pulls away from the mixer bowl, 10 to 15 minutes.
Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and/or a tea towel, and let sit at warm room temperature (75 to 27°C; 24 to 27°C) until doubled in size, 30 to 40 minutes.
Line a 13- by 46-cm rimmed baking sheet with parchment. Lightly flour the parchment; set aside.
On a lightly floured work surface, roll dough out to 0.5-cm thickness. Let rest for 10 minutes, until the tough is soft again and easy to handle.

Using a lightly floured 8-cm round cookie cutter, punch out 10 portions of dough; transfer to prepared baking sheet, cover loosely with a kitchen towel, and let rest for another 10 minutes, until the bread is soft and slightly risen.

Preheat air fryer to 175°C (350°F). Arrange as many pitas as you can fit on bottom of air fryer basket, spacing each about 2.5 cm apart. Bake until puffed and slightly golden around the edges, about 5 minutes. Repeat with remaining pita.

schema_metadata.keywords: pita bread, pita, pita bread recipe, how to make pita bread, homemade pita bread

description: With a few pantry staples and an air fryer, you can have wonderfully fluffy pita ready for stuffing, scooping, and snacking whenever you want—no trips to the bakery necessary.
notes:
Total time, including resting: 3 hr 4 min.

Optional substitutions: granulated sugar → honey

Notes: If you don't have a cookie cutter, use the rim of a round glass to portion the pita dough.
To make a larger pita, increase bake time as needed. An 20-cm pita will take about 7 minutes to make in the air fryer.

Make-ahead and storage: Once cooled, the pita can be stored in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 days, or refrigerated for up to 5 days. Pita can be frozen in a zip-top bag with parchment between each pita. Reheat directly from frozen in the air fryer. Alternatively, frozen pita can be wrapped tightly in foil and reheated in a 175°C until warmed through.
author: Nermine Mansour
